g|1:0.name: N이에요/예요 (to be)
g|1:0.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:0.why: 학생 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so it takes 이에요.

g|1:1.name: N이/가 아니에요 (not to be)
g|1:1.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:1.why: 아니에요 takes 이/가, and 가방 ends in a consonant, so 가방이.

g|1:2.name: Topic particle 은/는
g|1:2.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:2.why: After a vowel the topic particle is 는: 저는.

g|1:3.name: Present tense -아요/어요
g|1:3.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:3.why: 먹- has the vowel ㅓ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어요.

g|1:4.name: Object particle 을/를
g|1:4.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:4.why: After a vowel the object particle is 를: 커피를.

g|1:5.name: 있어요/없어요 (have, there is)
g|1:5.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:5.why: To say you don't have something, use 없어요, not 안 있어요.

g|1:6.name: N 주세요 (please give me)
g|1:6.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:6.why: To ask for something, put 주세요 after the item.

g|1:7.name: Negation with 안
g|1:7.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|1:7.why: 안 goes right before the verb: 안 먹어요.

g|2:0.name: Past tense -았/었어요
g|2:0.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.

g|2:1.name: Future -(으)ㄹ 거예요
g|2:1.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:1.gloss: I'm going to meet a friend tomorrow.
g|2:1.why: 만나- ends in a vowel, so -ㄹ 거예요: 만날 거예요 (spelled 거예요).

g|2:2.name: -고 싶어요 (want to)
g|2:2.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:2.gloss: I want to go to Jeju Island.

g|2:3.name: -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요/없어요 (can, cannot)
g|2:3.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:3.gloss: I can speak a little Korean.
g|2:3.why: 하- ends in a vowel, so -ㄹ 수 있어요: 할 수 있어요.

g|2:4.name: -고 (and then)
g|2:4.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:4.gloss: I washed and then had breakfast.
g|2:4.why: To link actions, put -고 right on the stem: 씻고.

g|2:5.name: -(으)러 가요 (go to do)
g|2:5.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:5.gloss: I'm going to the market to buy fruit.
g|2:5.why: With 가다/오다, purpose is -(으)러; 사- ends in a vowel → 사러.

g|2:6.name: -(으)ㄹ까요? (shall we)
g|2:6.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:6.why: Shall we = -(으)ㄹ까요; 먹- ends in a consonant → 먹을까요.

g|2:7.name: Place particles 에 and 에서
g|2:7.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|2:7.why: Where an action happens takes 에서 (에 is where something is or goes).

g|3:0.name: -(으)니까 (because, so — with suggestions)
g|3:0.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:0.gloss: It's raining, so let's take a taxi.
g|3:0.why: With a suggestion (let's …), use -(으)니까, not -아서 or -기 때문에.

g|3:1.name: -아서/어서 (because, then)
g|3:1.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:1.gloss: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
g|3:1.why: -아서/어서 never takes past -았/었-: 피곤해서, not 피곤했어서.

g|3:2.name: -는데 (background, contrast)
g|3:2.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:2.gloss: I went to the store, but it was closed.
g|3:2.why: Background with a verb is -는데; past 갔 + 는데 → 갔는데.

g|3:3.name: -(으)면 (if, when)
g|3:3.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:3.gloss: If you have time, call me.
g|3:3.why: 있- ends in a consonant, so -으면: 있으면.

g|3:4.name: -(으)ㄹ게요 (I will, promise)
g|3:4.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:4.why: The promise ending -(으)ㄹ게요 is spelled 게, never 께.

g|3:5.name: -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 (have done before)
g|3:5.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:5.gloss: I have been to Busan before.
g|3:5.why: Experience uses the past modifier -(으)ㄴ: 가 본 적이 있어요.

g|3:6.name: -기 때문에 (because of)
g|3:6.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:6.gloss: I have an exam, so I can't go out.
g|3:6.why: Verb + -기 때문에 (a noun takes 때문에 directly).

g|3:7.name: Casual speech 반말 -아/어
g|3:7.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|3:7.gloss: (to a close friend) Where are you going?
g|3:7.why: Between close friends, drop 요: 어디 가?

g|4:0.name: Honorific -(으)시- with 께서, 드리다, 여쭤보다
g|4:0.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:0.why: 자다 has its own honorific verb: 주무시다 → 주무세요.

g|4:1.name: Reported speech -대요/-래요
g|4:1.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:1.gloss: (I heard) she says she's busy today.
g|4:1.why: Reporting what someone said is -대요 (from -다고 해요); -데요 is for what you saw yourself.

g|4:2.name: -더라고요 (what I noticed)
g|4:2.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:2.gloss: (I went and found that) the food there was really good.
g|4:2.why: What you noticed yourself is -더라고요 (spelled 더, not 드).

g|4:3.name: -잖아요 (you know)
g|4:3.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:3.why: A noun ending in a consonant takes 이잖아요 (spelled 잖아요).

g|4:4.name: -거든요 (giving the reason)
g|4:4.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:4.gloss: (Why am I tired?) I worked late yesterday.
g|4:4.why: Giving the reason is -거든요; yesterday needs past: 했 + 거든요.

g|4:5.name: -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다 (almost)
g|4:5.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:5.why: Almost = -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다, always in the past.

g|4:6.name: -는 바람에 (because of an unexpected event)
g|4:6.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:6.gloss: The alarm didn't go off, so I was late.
g|4:6.why: It is always -는 바람에, even for past events.

g|4:7.name: -(으)ㄹ 텐데 (probably, I'm concerned that)
g|4:7.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|4:7.gloss: He's probably busy, so call him later.
g|4:7.why: A guess with concern is -(으)ㄹ 텐데 (spelled 텐데).

g|5:0.name: -다 보니 (as I kept doing, it turned out)
g|5:0.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:0.gloss: As we kept talking, we became close.
g|5:0.why: -다 보니 goes on the plain stem, without -았/었-.

g|5:1.name: -는 셈이다 (it amounts to)
g|5:1.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:1.why: Something already done is -(으)ㄴ 셈이다 (spelled 셈).

g|5:2.name: -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬다 (I should have)
g|5:2.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:2.gloss: I should have brought an umbrella.
g|5:2.why: Regret is -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬다, in the past and spelled 걸.

g|5:3.name: -기는 하는데 (it is true, but)
g|5:3.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:3.gloss: I do exercise, but not often.
g|5:3.why: With a verb it is -기는 하는데 (with an adjective, -기는 한데).
g|5:3.line: 운동을 하기는 하는데 자주 안 해요.

g|5:4.name: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다 (pretend)
g|5:4.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:4.why: Pretend is -는 척하다; here in the past: 척했어요.

g|5:5.name: -(으)ㄹ 만하다 (it's understandable, worth it)
g|5:5.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:5.why: Worth doing is -(으)ㄹ 만하다: 보- → 볼 만해요.

g|5:6.name: -더니 (contrast or result from what you saw)
g|5:6.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:6.gloss: He studied hard, and then he passed.
g|5:6.why: What you saw him do, then the result: -더니 (spelled 더).

g|5:7.name: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 (in case, worried that)
g|5:7.ask: Pick the Korean that fits the meaning.
g|5:7.gloss: I left early in case I'd be late.
g|5:7.why: Worried that = -(으)ㄹ까 봐: 늦- → 늦을까 봐.
